hasyncVersion.note: #459 audited every endpoint sharing OSPFv3's `Response json.RawMessage` envelope pattern and left this one unwrapped deliberately, not for lack of a body type to point at. hasyncVersionResponse.Response is genuinely polymorphic on the wire: an object ({"firmware":{...}}) only when HA is configured and the peer answers; a bare JSON boolean (`false`) on the overwhelming majority of installs (single-node, HA unconfigured — see HasyncStatusController.php's exception path); JSON null on some error paths. Reflecting through it as an object would misdescribe the common case as a schema conflict rather than widen an unverified path, which is the opposite of what #459 is for. PRUNE TRIGGER: if a future OPNsense release collapses this to one shape, or if per-field polymorphic kinds are ever supported by FieldKind, register an envelopeDescent here like the other FRR/Tor endpoints.

quaggaOspfInterface.note: #459 audited every endpoint sharing OSPFv3's `Response json.RawMessage` envelope pattern; this one is deliberately left as a bare envelope rather than unwrapped. frr.go's FetchFRROSPFInterfaces decodes TWO candidate shapes for the same endpoint: FRR>=8 wraps per-interface data in {"interfaces": {...}} (frrOSPFInterfaceWrapped, confirmed live against this box's FRR 10.3), while older FRR returns the flat per-interface map directly at the top level (frrOSPFInterfaceEntry map) per the plugin's own doc comments — but that flat shape has never itself been confirmed live. Registering an envelopeDescent requires naming ONE Inner type; picking the wrapped shape would silently assert the flat shape doesn't exist, and picking the flat shape would misdescribe the one shape actually verified. PRUNE TRIGGER: confirm which shape(s) a live box in the support window actually sends (dev-box FRR is 10.3, already wrapped-only), then register an envelopeDescent — same treatment as quaggaOspfv3Interface below, which has no such ambiguity.

keaLeases6.note: DHCPv6 lease rows were the last source-derived Kea surface; closed 2026-07-25. ROOT CAUSE of the long-standing gap, recorded so it is not re-investigated: the Proxmox host kernel is booted with ipv6.disable=1, so /proc/sys/net/ipv6 does not exist in ANY namespace on that host and NO LXC on it can ever run a DHCPv6 client. This is a host-kernel property, not container privilege - the earlier #227 conclusion. Only a VM (own kernel) can hold a v6 lease; bridge-level L2 forwarding is unaffected. REGRESSION TRIGGER: these rows expire within the lease lifetime (~4000s) if that VM is stopped. Also note keaLeases4 is currently EMPTY (no DHCPv4 client on the test VLAN) despite a 2026-07-13 capture, so a v4 lease row is now the weaker side.
